title: Eviction safeguards and variant hedging for regional failover
creator: Marco Chen
description:
Goal: Implement a coordinated regional failover orchestration feature that minimizes user-facing disruption during region outages by (1) preventing large-scale eviction storms through eviction safeguards and capacity gating, (2) hedging model availability with tiered fallback variants (quantized/distilled) chosen by routing policy, and (3) ensuring warm-standby readiness via deterministic prefill probes and KV cache priming.

Background: Existing warm-standby activations occasionally trigger capacity-driven evictions when traffic is shifted aggressively. In parallel, naive fallback to smaller model variants can cause quality regressions without a transparent routing policy and graceful degradation window. We need a single orchestration layer that coordinates region-level decisions (activate standby, throttle cutover), node-level eviction policies (graceful drain thresholds, preemption-safe buckets), and model-variant selection rules (latency-first, quality-first, or cost-constrained hedges).

Scope: Implementation focuses on hosted and dedicated fleets for regions with active warm-standby configured. Private deployments may use the same primitives but are out of scope for this ticket (follow-up). Work includes controller logic, new readiness scoring, API toggles for rollout, telemetry, and a small console UX flag for emergency manual trigger.
acceptance_criteria: Readiness score computed for each standby region and exposed via API and console (score in 0-100)
Failover activation respects 'eviction_safeguard' policy: will not shift more than configured percentage of traffic until capacity gating passes
Fallback model variant selector can be configured per-route and supports at least three policies: quality-first, latency-first, cost-constrained
KV cache priming runs before traffic cutover and achieves >60% cache hit rate on synthetic validation workload within 5 minutes in 90% of runs
Automated canary cutover (1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) proceeds only when SLOs (p95 latency, error rate) stay within configured thresholds at each step
New telemetry (eviction events, prefill success, variant switch) is available in the console and exported to logs/dashboards
Runbook steps for emergency rollback are documented and validated in a tabletop exercise
implementation_plan: Design API: /regions/{r}/readiness (GET) and /failover/actions (POST) with eviction_safeguard and variant_policy payloads
Controller: add 'eviction_safety' module that computes move quotas per region based on capacity and recent eviction rate
Prefill job: deterministic KV-prefill that replays hot prefixes for configured routes; tag prefill runs with correlation-id
Variant selector: policy engine that evaluates model fingerprint, quantization level, latency/quality profile and returns chosen variant
Integrations: console toggle, alerting (PagerDuty), metrics (Prometheus/Grafana) for readiness and prefill progress
Tests: unit + integration harness for controller decisions, simulation harness to run capacity-constrained cutover scenarios
Docs: update runbook, add API docs and sample curl/SDK usage
test_plan: Synthetic failover simulation: run 10-day traffic replay across three regions, force region A offline and verify staggered cutover obeys quotas
Chaos run: randomly drop 20% of capacity in region B during cutover and assert no eviction cascade exceeds threshold
Quality regression tests: when fallback to distilled model occurs, run 50 curated prompts and ensure average BLEU/ROUGE delta within configured guardrails
Prefill validation: measure KV hit-rate and cold-start latency delta before and after prefill for targeted routes
Canary gating: automated pipeline that advances traffic only when p95 and error_rate both pass checks for 5 minutes at each stage
rollback_plan: If metrics cross rollback thresholds (p95 > configured OR error_rate spike > configured OR eviction_rate increases beyond 2x baseline), immediately stop cutover, shift traffic back to primary region via priority routing, and run background prefill with degraded concurrency. After rollback, create postmortem and a task to harden failing stage.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overly conservative eviction_safeguard delaying failover and increasing customer impact. Mitigation: provide emergency override with authorization and gradual auto-escalation policy tied to incident severity.

Risk: Fallback model causes subtle correctness regressions. Mitigation: pair fallback with per-route evaluation sets and automatic regression alerts; allow 'quality-first' policy to avoid fallback for critical routes.
Risk: Prefill floods network when misconfigured. Mitigation: prefill rate limits, backoff on errors, and affinity-based prefill to minimize cross-region bandwidth.
Risk: Metric noise causes canary flapping. Mitigation: require stability window and minimal sample size before advancing canary steps; use aggregated percentiles.
Risk: Console toggle abused. Mitigation: RBAC for emergency toggle and audit log entries for all manual activations.
